{
  "candidate_rtl": "`timescale 1ns / 1ps
`default_nettype none

module priority_encoder #(
    parameter WIDTH = 4,
    parameter LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY = 0
)(
    input  wire [WIDTH-1:0] input_unencoded,
    output wire output_valid,
    output wire [$clog2(WIDTH)-1:0] output_encoded,
    output wire [WIDTH-1:0] output_unencoded
);

parameter LEVELS = WIDTH > 2 ? $clog2(WIDTH) : 1;
parameter W = 2**LEVELS;

generate
    if (WIDTH == 256 && LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY == 0) begin : fast_256
        wire [15:0] group_valid;
        wire [15:0] group_enable;
        wire [15:0] group_winner;
        wire [255:0] local_winner;
        wire [15:0] low_terms [3:0];
        wire [15:0] high_terms [3:0];

        genvar g, j, b;
        for (g = 0; g < 16; g = g + 1) begin : groups
            wire [15:0] x;
            wire [3:0] local_code;
            assign x = input_unencoded[g*16 +: 16];
            assign group_valid[g] = |x;
            if (g == 15) begin : top_group
                assign group_enable[g] = 1'b1;
            end else begin : other_group
                assign group_enable[g] = ~(|group_valid[15:g+1]);
            end
            assign group_winner[g] = group_valid[g] & group_enable[g];

            for (j = 0; j < 16; j = j + 1) begin : positions
                if (j == 15) begin : top_position
                    assign local_winner[g*16+j] = x[j];
                end else begin : other_position
                    assign local_winner[g*16+j] = x[j] & ~(|x[15:j+1]);
                end
                if (g == 0 && j == 0) begin : zero_position
                    // Index zero wins both for input bit zero alone and for no input.
                    assign output_unencoded[g*16+j] = ~(|input_unencoded[255:1]);
                end else begin : nonzero_position
                    assign output_unencoded[g*16+j] =
                        local_winner[g*16+j] & group_enable[g];
                end
            end

            for (b = 0; b < 4; b = b + 1) begin : code_bits
                wire [15:0] local_terms;
                for (j = 0; j < 16; j = j + 1) begin : terms
                    if ((j & (1 << b)) != 0) begin : included
                        assign local_terms[j] = local_winner[g*16+j];
                    end else begin : excluded
                        assign local_terms[j] = 1'b0;
                    end
                end
                assign local_code[b] = |local_terms;
                assign low_terms[b][g] = local_code[b] & group_enable[g];
                if ((g & (1 << b)) != 0) begin : high_included
                    assign high_terms[b][g] = group_winner[g];
                end else begin : high_excluded
                    assign high_terms[b][g] = 1'b0;
                end
            end
        end

        for (b = 0; b < 4; b = b + 1) begin : encoded_bits
            assign output_encoded[b] = |low_terms[b];
            assign output_encoded[b+4] = |high_terms[b];
        end
        assign output_valid = |group_valid;
    end else begin : generic_encoder
        reg [$clog2(WIDTH)-1:0] code;
        integer k;
        always @* begin
            if (LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY) begin
                code = W-1;
                for (k = WIDTH-1; k >= 0; k = k-1)
                    if (input_unencoded[k]) code = k;
            end else begin
                code = 0;
                for (k = 0; k < WIDTH; k = k+1)
                    if (input_unencoded[k]) code = k;
            end
        end
        assign output_valid = |input_unencoded;
        assign output_encoded = code;
        assign output_unencoded = 1 << output_encoded;
    end
endgenerate

endmodule

`default_nettype wire
",
  "bottleneck": "The supplied measured maximum arrival is 2.60 ns. All three reported paths terminate at one-hot outputs and share a substantial upstream cone, including a buffer, a 0.58 ns mux2i stage, and a subsequent 0.47 ns complex-gate stage. Together with the original RTL's encoded-result-to-one-hot shift, this supports investigating shared priority-selection logic followed by decoding and fanout as the bottleneck. The paths do not establish an exact RTL-to-cell correspondence or prove that decoding alone dominates.",
  "rewrite": "Use sixteen groups of sixteen inputs. Within each group, compute highest-set-bit winner terms directly using higher-bit reductions. In parallel, compute group occupancy and higher-group exclusion. Drive each nonzero-index one-hot output directly from its local winner and group enable, without passing through the eight-bit encoded result. Generate encoded bits with masked OR reductions: the high four bits from winning groups, and the low four bits from enabled local codes. Compute output_unencoded[0] directly as the NOR of input bits 255 through 1, preserving the required invalid-input result. Retain the original module interface, parameter names and defaults, with a generic combinational fallback outside the optimized instance.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "A reduction from the 2.60 ns baseline is plausible because the one-hot outputs no longer wait for a complete encoded result and its decoder. An exploratory target is approximately 1.8–2.3 ns, about 12–31% lower arrival, but this is a hypothesis, not a measured result. The encoded-output reduction trees or group-enable fanout could instead become critical. Only mapping and STA under the supplied fixed flow can establish the actual gain.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "The rewrite exchanges the shared encoder/decoder structure for local exclusion logic, group exclusion logic, and masked OR trees. Sharing of local winners between encoded and one-hot outputs should help contain area, but buffering of group enables and duplicated reduction logic are risks. No mapped area or electrical-check result is available for this candidate. Acceptance requires mapped area at or below 8862.124480 um^2, zero max-slew and max-capacitance violations, full equivalence, and improved maximum data arrival under the specified mapping policy.",
  "functional_boundaries": "For WIDTH=256 and LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY=0, every binary input is permitted. For nonzero input, exactly the highest set index is selected; output_valid is one, output_encoded is that index, and output_unencoded has exactly that bit set. For zero input, all local winners and encoded terms are zero, output_valid=0, output_encoded=0, and output_unencoded=256'b1. No outputs are treated as don't-cares. The circuit has no clocks, state, latches, assumptions, or input restrictions. Equivalence has not been run here; the full fixed-instance proof remains mandatory."
